title: AI barely registers with midterm voters — campaigns run on it anyway
summary: Under one percent of voters name AI as their deciding issue, yet data centers are an attack line in nearly half the battleground races; Ada and Alan work out how both are true and what a Democratic House would do. Then an Anthropic manager drops the coding interview on his teams, against an automation-deskilling warning and Proton's cancelled AI 're-interviews', and the week in review.

topics: Is AI a midterm election issue (Transformer, 30 Oct 2026): under 0.5% in NYT/Siena name AI or data centers as most important issue (joint 19th), 3% in Reuters/Ipsos; DCCC messaging references AI/data centers in almost half of key battleground races (attacks over an $80B data-center tax-break bill); WaPo analysis ranks tech/AI sixth in Democratic ad spending; Trump-backed super PAC attacks Democrats' data-center links; Florida AG Uthmeier advertises his OpenAI lawsuit; Montana ad with Paul Christiano; AI super PACs $78.5M on federal candidates, pro-development outspent safety $8M to $6.9M in general-election races; Brad Carson's 'stitching together intense voters'; taught Converse's issue publics; AI rides on corruption, jobs and electricity bills. What a Democratic House would do: Casar's hearings pledge; Raskin and Garcia demand preservation of White House chatbot prompts under the Presidential Records Act, briefing by Nov 11, citing Time's Grok/Maduro report. Watch: data-center-attack races vs district baseline.

Felix Rieseberg drops the coding interview on his Anthropic teams ('Hunger beats tenure', 27 Oct 2026): 'laid the traditional coding interview to rest', once 'a weak but useful predictor'; React challenge vs assembly; no replacement yet ('I haven't quite gotten there yet'), portfolios showing taste, empathy, principled thinking; junior advice (manager's manager's goals, weekend prototype, one idea); Morris and Zhao's weekend Claude Code prototype shipped ~8 days later; not a company-wide Anthropic policy. Countered with SigNoz's deskilling piece (Bainbridge 1983 'Ironies of Automation', endoscopist detection 28% to 22%, never-skilling), Atlassian 2026 survey via LeadDev (68% to 25% saving 10+ hours/week; 65% fixing AI code; 60% say AI usage treated as productivity signal vs 42% of leaders with the right metric), Proton cancelling AI 're-interviews' after 404 Media, Amazon adding AI usage to engineer expectations. Unresolved: Alan says taste is exercised not eroded; Ada wants no-model fire drills.

Sunday week in review (26 Oct-1 Nov): receipts demanded — money (S-1, Alphabet, OpenAI round, Anthropic junk-rating forecast), OpenAI's containment account with admitted gaps, and measurements made through the thing measured (ETH proofs, AA v5, Claude Enterprise reports, hidden-lean study).

dives.why_it_matters: Policy and election watchers need to know that AI wins votes only through data centers, bills and corruption, and that a flipped House would bring AI-CEO hearings and records demands rather than new law.
